hard_gates.evidence: I ran 3 full verifies of 72fa2f65 through the verify slots, compose project c-p12-jobs-r3, ports 21250-21261. All 3 failed. Erp.Gates.Tests.G1.G1HttpIsolationTests.Tenant_A_cannot_reach_tenant_B_through_any_endpoint failed in all 3 runs, each time because one of the gate's GET requests passed the HttpClient's 100-second timeout. The failing step was different each time. Run 1: TenantActivity.ReadRoundAsync in WritePairsPhaseAsync, 1 h 3 m, peak load 120. Run 2: ListAnswers.WalkTogetherAsync, 1 h 42 m, mean load 25.7. Run 3: TenantActivity.RunConcurrentlyAsync, the concurrent reader for tenant B, 1 h 41 m. Run 3's message: 'The request was canceled due to the configured HttpClient.Timeout of 100 seconds elapsing.' It failed at about 14:35Z, when the machine load was 3 to 8 (verify/run3/verify-load-samples, 10-minute means 3.3 to 3.6). Load does not explain a single GET hanging for 100 s, so I count this as a real failing test. The other failures were load-related and pass when run alone. Run 2: harness tests causation.test.mjs:575, guard.test.mjs:1206 and measured-part.test.mjs:139 'control C3'; all pass alone (harness-3-tests-alone.log). biggest_gap.title: The full suite does not pass: the G1 HTTP isolation gate fails at this commit because a GET hangs for more than 100 s, in 3 of 3 runs and once on a quiet machine
biggest_gap.detail: Erp.Gates.Tests.G1.G1HttpIsolationTests.Tenant_A_cannot_reach_tenant_B_through_any_endpoint failed in all 3 of my full verifies of 72fa2f65. Each time, one of the gate's GET requests hit HttpClient's 100-second timeout, at a different step each time: the read round after the write pairs, the paired list walk (ListAnswers.WalkTogetherAsync), and tenant B's concurrent reader (TenantActivity.RunConcurrentlyAsync). The third failure came at about 14:35Z while the machine load was 3 to 8. At 18:41Z (local time) the Gates test host had used 1 h 51 m of processor time, but over a 20 s sample it used 0.25 s and the test database committed only about 3 transactions a second, so the test was waiting, not computing. A GET that waits 100 s on an idle machine is a hang, not load. Until it is found, no full verify of this commit passes, and the isolation proof for every surface, p12's included, is not complete. The gate does not report which request timed out: the label passed to TenantActivity.SendAsync is lost in the TaskCanceledException. On the 100,000-job demo, I timed p12's GETs and the reports that the concurrent reader also hits; all answered in under 8 s (attack/get-timing.txt), so the hanging request is probably something these reports did not reach. The commit also brings p00 round 16's session prefetch (ISessionPrefetch) and p10 round 3's changes, so the cause may lie outside p12. The fix starts by making the gate name the request that timed out, then finding and fixing the hang.

other_findings: Scope (cancellation): cancelling a running job can fail with a false conflict. JobQueue.CancelAsync loads the job and saves it with EF's optimistic version check. The worker updates the row on every progress report (at most every 250 ms) and on every 2 s heartbeat. If one of those writes lands between the cancel's read and its save, the API answers 409 'Someone else changed this record after you opened it. Reload it and try again.', and the job then runs to the end. In the browser on a loaded machine, Alt+K on a running self-check (12 steps of 900 ms) showed exactly that message in the panel, and the job finished Done. Through the API: 1 of 12 cancels at load about 60 (attack/cancel-probe-fast.txt) and 1 of 30 at load about 6 (attack/cancel-probe-quiet.txt) answered 409, and those jobs ended 'succeeded'. Long jobs that report progress often, such as imports, will hit this more. The fix: an atomic UPDATE ... SET cancel_requested = true WHERE id = @id AND status NOT IN (finished) (plus status = cancelled when queued), or a retry on DbUpdateConcurrencyException; a module test that cancels while progress is being written. Related: 5 of 30 cancels that answered 200 in the last part of a 1-second job ended 'succeeded' with cancel_requested true (attack/cancel-probe-quiet-db.txt), because a request after the last throttled report is never seen. That fits 'ends when it does', but the panel then shows Done after the user cancelled.

[route: p00-foundation] The G1 HTTP gate loses the request label when a request times out (TenantActivity.SendAsync and ListAnswers.GetAsync throw a bare TaskCanceledException), so a hang cannot be traced to its endpoint without a debugger. Put the label and path in the failure message.

The builder's comparison driver for see-and-rerun-job still errors at the bar volume (compare-run1.log). In round 3 it waits until the list is filtered, but Enter after a search matching more than 10,000 rows ('Self-check of the job queue' matches 24,623; the server sends ranked:false) only moves the focus into the list (kernel ListView afterSearchEnter, p05). The driver passes only in verify's 2,000-row health check. My driver (compare-ours-driver-critic-fix.mjs) shows the real expert path: type 'self', Enter, arrow past the newest unfinished rows, Enter, Alt+R.

Fixed since round 2 and confirmed in the browser: the Arabic job title on the Arabic list and panel (08, 09); the schedules' Kind column shows the kind's name in the screen's language (07, 10); the seeded schedule name is in one language; Ctrl+Enter in the Start dialog starts the job (02 to 03); the job panel's note now reads 'Read only: Jobs cannot be edited. Use Run again or Cancel.'; live progress (33%, then 66 to 75%), output download (self-check.txt), Run again (Alt+R) and a failed job's error all work by keyboard. A cron schedule '* * * * *' queued its job at the next minute, which the scheduler ran and finished as succeeded (attack/cron-probe.txt).

Demo data: most seeded jobs are of kinds no module registers ('Load the daily rate file', 'Close the accounting period', 'Post depreciation entries', 'Send payment reminders'). A seeded failed clean-up job shows 'Tries 2 of 2' but no tries table, with the generic error 'The job stopped with an error. (jobs.seed)' (06 screenshot). On the Arabic screen, the seeded alnoor schedule is named in English because the workspace's first administrator works in English (10 screenshot).

Still as in round 2: the worker container holds the erp_owner connection string (compose ConnectionStrings__Owner) to find workspaces with work. erp_owner is NOBYPASSRLS and RLS is forced, so I saw no leak, but every future module's job handler will run in a process holding the table owner's role.
